q: In Homotopy Type Theory (HoTT), the univalence axiom (Voevodsky) states that for types A and B:
opts: A = B iff they are isomorphic sets
The type (A = B) is equivalent to the type of equivalences (A ≃ B)
A = B iff they have the same cardinality
exp: Univalence: (A =_U B) ≃ (A ≃ B). This means equivalence of types is the same as identity of types—formalizing the informal mathematical practice of treating isomorphic objects as identical. It implies function extensionality as a corollary.
